correctness.rationale: On each subtree I, restricted Haar Parseval and binary x_j²=x_j imply s_I-s_I²/|I| equals a sum determined by internal detail magnitudes. Thus a competing subtree total can only be observed s_I or its complement |I|-s_I. At fixed parent total, swapping child sums is possible for nonzero contrast exactly when s_I=|I|/2; complementation within the children bijects the two solutions, yielding a product recurrence and |F(x)|=2^{b(x)} by induction. A second induction gives b_I<=min(s_I,|I|-s_I), saturated by ones in distinct lowest adjacent pairs, and equality at N/2 forces all higher details zero. Independently enumerated every binary vector at N=2,4,8,16, grouping by complete signed-total/labelled-absolute-detail data; for N=16, all 65,536 signals, 3,256 fibers with exact histogram 2,85,453,862,921,650,238,44,1 at sizes 1..256 powers of two, all fixed-weight maxima confirmed. The all-N conclusion rests on induction.
